name: Gunner
summary: Most military and some civilian Vehicles have built-in weapons. Any weapon not controlled by the Vehicle Pilot or Copilot requires a Gunner to operate. A Vehicle can have as many Gunners as it has Gunner positions.

fields.automatic_misses: If you roll a Natural 1 on your attack, you automatically miss.
fields.base_attack_bonus: Use the Base Attack Bonus of the Gunner (which, in some cases, may be the Vehicle Pilot).
fields.critical_hits: When you roll a Natural 20 on your attack, you automatically hit the target and deal double damage. When using a Vehicle Weapon, you cannot apply any effect that causes an automatic Natural 20 or automatic Critical Hit (such as spending a Destiny Point or using the Jedi Master’s Serenity class feature), unless a rule specifies that it can be used with Vehicle Attacks.
fields.damage_multiplier: After rolling the weapon damage dice, multiply the result by the listed Damage Multiplier. For example, when you fire a Vehicle Weapon that deals 6d10x2 damage, roll 6d10 and multiply the result by 2.
fields.intelligence_modifier: A Vehicle's computer improves the accuracy of the Vehicle's Weapon Systems, and the Vehicle's Intelligence score measures the quality of the computer.
fields.weapon_range_modifier: A Vehicle Weapon can attack a target at Point-Blank, Short, Medium, or Long Range.

name: Vehicle Pilot
summary: The Pilot of the Vehicle controls its movement. Most Vehicles have only one position from where it can be Piloted. fields.attacking_in_a_dogfight: Make an opposed Pilot check as a Standard Action, if you succeed on the opposed check, you may make a single Vehicle Attack as a Swift Action.

fields.base_attack_bonus: Use the Base Attack Bonus of the Gunner (which, in some cases, may be the Vehicle Pilot).
fields.critical_hits: When you roll a Natural 20 on your attack, you automatically hit the target and deal double damage. When using a Vehicle Weapon, you cannot apply any effect that causes an automatic Natural 20 or automatic Critical Hit (such as spending a Destiny Point or using the Jedi Master’s Serenity class feature), unless a rule specifies that it can be used with Vehicle Attacks.
fields.damage_multiplier: After rolling the weapon damage dice, multiply the result by the listed Damage Multiplier. For example, when you fire a Vehicle Weapon that deals 6d10x2 damage, roll 6d10 and multiply the result by 2.
fields.disengaging_from_a_dogfight: Make an opposed Pilot check as a Move Action, if you succeed on the opposed check, you successfully Disengage from the Dogfight, and may move a number of squares equal to your Vehicle's Speed.
fields.firing_into_a_dogfight: If another Vehicle fires into a Dogfight, it takes a -5 penalty on its attack roll, unless the Gunner has the Precise Shot feat.
fields.intelligence_modifier: A Vehicle's computer improves the accuracy of the Vehicle's Weapon Systems, and the Vehicle's Intelligence score measures the quality of the computer.
fields.starship_scale: Collisions are easier to avoid at Starship Scale. If you succeed on the Pilot check to Avoid Collision in Starship Scale, no Collision occurs.
fields.trained_pilot: If you are Trained in the Pilot skill, your Vehicle instead gains a +5 dodge bonus to its Reflex Defense, with you and all Gunners on your Vehicle taking a -5 penalty on attack rolls; or a +10 dodge bonus if you choose to make no attacks on your turn.
